raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving Strawberry Fields behind, head for American Museum of Natural History, about a 15-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"A plaque back there named 121 nations; the halls ahead gather the spectrum of life.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Come in through the Gilder Center, and the lobby stops you — walls of pale concrete curving like a canyon.","source_id":"92ef9bc6-5719-49b7-9b20-79b9a8a418de","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"That sinuous look, echoing the canyons of the American Southwest, came from spraying structural concrete straight onto rebar.","source_id":"92ef9bc6-5719-49b7-9b20-79b9a8a418de","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"But here's the thing about this place, founded back in 1869: it has never been only a museum.","source_id":"da442c49-2144-4556-9ac4-8a51d2d8d836","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"It's also the country's preeminent private science lab, and its research and its galleries feed each other — which is why what's on display can actually change.","source_id":"da442c49-2144-4556-9ac4-8a51d2d8d836","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"A few years ago, scientists worked out that dinosaurs didn't drag their tails along the ground.","source_id":"da442c49-2144-4556-9ac4-8a51d2d8d836","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"They held them up, waving in the air, as they walked.","source_id":"da442c49-2144-4556-9ac4-8a51d2d8d836","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"So the curators took the famous skeletons apart, bone by bone, and rebuilt them with tails raised.","source_id":"da442c49-2144-4556-9ac4-8a51d2d8d836","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Then they set one over a slab of Texas riverbed lined with fossilized footprints — and not one tail-drag mark among them.","source_id":"da442c49-2144-4556-9ac4-8a51d2d8d836","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"It's a peephole into how a scientific theory actually comes to be.","source_id":"da442c49-2144-4556-9ac4-8a51d2d8d836","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"That Gilder Center opened in 2023 at a cost of $431 million, and it holds about a twelfth of the whole collection across 230,000 square feet.","source_id":"92ef9bc6-5719-49b7-9b20-79b9a8a418de","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Inside there's an insectarium, a butterfly vivarium, open storage, and a 360-degree Invisible Worlds Theater about the networks that link all life.","source_id":"92ef9bc6-5719-49b7-9b20-79b9a8a418de","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Down on the first floor, the Hall of Biodiversity has a real showstopper.","source_id":"ccf63ec6-6a6d-498c-ad32-101906b31632","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"It's called \"The Spectrum of Life,\" a wall of specimens lit up almost psychedelic.","source_id":"ccf63ec6-6a6d-498c-ad32-101906b31632","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Close by, a rain-forest diorama pipes in video, sound, and even smell, so you feel like you've walked inside one.","source_id":"ccf63ec6-6a6d-498c-ad32-101906b31632","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The message underneath is plain: Earth's life-forms are varied, tangled together, and worth preserving.","source_id":"ccf63ec6-6a6d-498c-ad32-101906b31632","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Elsewhere there are gem galleries and an IMAX screen.","source_id":"12df5324-3f70-4e0d-b2a5-3bdfca80d0bc","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The Hall of Ocean Life turns on ecology and conservation, all of it under a 94-foot blue whale hung from the ceiling.","source_id":"12df5324-3f70-4e0d-b2a5-3bdfca80d0bc","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"At one entrance stands a 63-foot canoe, carved in the 1800s by the Haida people.","source_id":"12df5324-3f70-4e0d-b2a5-3bdfca80d0bc","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"They came from the coast of British Columbia.","source_id":"12df5324-3f70-4e0d-b2a5-3bdfca80d0bc","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Up on the third floor, the Margaret Mead Hall of Pacific Peoples carries the work of the anthropologist it's named for.","source_id":"18a5355d-b178-4488-b6fc-5953a77b60c8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"She lived from 1901 to 1978 and spent most of that life in the museum's own anthropology department.","source_id":"18a5355d-b178-4488-b6fc-5953a77b60c8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The hall roams the myriad cultures of the South Pacific islands, from Polynesia to Micronesia.","source_id":"18a5355d-b178-4488-b6fc-5953a77b60c8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Its wood-and-bark masks from Papua New Guinea are among the highlights.","source_id":"18a5355d-b178-4488-b6fc-5953a77b60c8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Got kids along? The Discovery Room lets them dig for dinosaur bones, chase a scavenger hunt, and peer through microscopes.","source_id":"ea3947c3-c2fb-4ae8-b866-4d13b710a04b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"It runs on timed free tickets, and they run out, so grab one early.","source_id":"ea3947c3-c2fb-4ae8-b866-4d13b710a04b","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"That's the walk — the museum where even the dinosaurs got their tails lifted.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1}]}
